integratedBehavior: The generated JSON Schema, TypeScript, and Python contract use immutable accepted/draft/superseded revision identities, stable content hashes, researcher rationale, explicit unknown/not-applicable states, closed autonomy and action vocabularies, local/approved egress invariants, and mode-compatible stopping rules. Intent acceptance, scope change, and external egress are outside machine authority.

The desktop provides guided required decisions, optional refinements, mode defaults, unresolved-state warnings, revision history, and impact acknowledgement. Incomplete or unsaved work remains a draft and cannot launch. Acceptance freezes one exact root, revision ID/number, full sha256 content hash, human rationale, confirmation, and 32-hex idempotency key before crossing the generated Core client.

An explicit Core problem is a definitive rejection. Transport loss or malformed/truncated response is treated as unresolved: the desktop retains and locks the exact command/key, makes no authority claim, and permits only exact reconciliation. Success or exact replay installs Core's returned accepted projection into current/history; the renderer never creates its own policy decision and launch remains disabled.

Core serializes project operations, accepts only the exact current decision-complete draft under stable local actor authority, persists revision, acceptance decision, provenance, outbox, and idempotency atomically, and reconstructs immutable accepted history after restart. Failed acceptance leaves the prior accepted revision authoritative.

Every policy evaluation resolves and caches only the newest contract-valid accepted revision, atomically replaces it after later acceptance, and prevents an older idempotent replay from rolling authority back. Systematic, theory, technical, hermeneutic, critical, and novelty modes receive governing-reference-bound working labels and required gates. Claim/publication, acceptance/scope, disallowed autonomy, local-only egress, absent accepted intent, and stopping confirmation fail closed with compact explanations.

Allow, deny, recommend-human, and require-confirmation outcomes append bounded content-free decision metadata and provenance in one transaction. Audit failure returns no usable policy result. The slice introduces no provider, hosted infrastructure, research-content telemetry, credential, dependency, or persistence-schema migration.
